title: Trivial zig-zags are zig-zags; functoriality of the zig-zag module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be double complexes of $R$-modules and $\Phi:A\to B$, $\Psi:B\to C$ morphisms of double complexes [def-weil-pbc-module-double-complex]. For $n\ge0$ let $T_n(-)=\bigoplus_{p+q=n,\,p,q\ge0}(-)_{p,q}$, $D_{n+1}:T_{n+1}(-)\to T_n(-)$, $D_{n+1}(b)_{p,q}=d_{p+1,q}(b_{p+1,q})+\delta_{p,q+1}(b_{p,q+1})$, the module of zig-zags $Z_n(-)\subseteq T_n(-)$, the module of trivial zig-zags $B_n(-)=\operatorname{im}D_{n+1}$ and the zig-zag module $\mathbf H_n(-)=Z_n(-)/(Z_n(-)\cap B_n(-))$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], and let $\Phi$ act on $T_n(A)$ componentwise, $\Phi(a)_{p,q}=\Phi_{p,q}(a_{p,q})$. Then for every $n\ge0$: (a) $B_n(A)\subseteq Z_n(A)$, so that $\mathbf H_n(A)=Z_n(A)/B_n(A)$; (b) $\Phi(Z_n(A))\subseteq Z_n(B)$ and $\Phi\circ D_{n+1}=D_{n+1}\circ\Phi$ as maps $T_{n+1}(A)\to T_n(B)$, hence $\Phi(B_n(A))\subseteq B_n(B)$; (c) there is a unique $R$-linear map $\mathbf H_n(\Phi):\mathbf H_n(A)\to\mathbf H_n(B)$ with $\mathbf H_n(\Phi)([a])=[\Phi(a)]$ for all $a\in Z_n(A)$; (d) $\mathbf H_n(\Psi\circ\Phi)=\mathbf H_n(\Psi)\circ\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$ and $\mathbf H_n(\mathrm{id}_A)=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf H_n(A)}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence; tags/tags: 00M1,algebra-lemma-no-spectral-sequence): statement, 'The isomorphisms are functorial with respect to morphisms of double complexes' (lines 18398-18412), and proof, lines 18416-18450 (the quotient $\mathbf H_i(A)$ of zig-zags by trivial zig-zags, 'Naturally, we divide out by trivial zig-zags'); the paragraph before it, lines 18391-18395 ('it is clear that this induces morphisms'). The source leaves (a)-(d) implicit.

proof.text: (a) $B_n(A)\subseteq Z_n(A)$. By [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], $Z_n(A)$ is the set of $a\in T_n(A)$ with $d_{r,s}(a_{r,s})=\delta_{r-1,s+1}(a_{r-1,s+1})$ for all $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $r+s=n$, and $B_n(A)=D_{n+1}(T_{n+1}(A))$. Let $b\in T_{n+1}(A)$ and $a=D_{n+1}(b)$, so $a_{r,s}=d_{r+1,s}(b_{r+1,s})+\delta_{r,s+1}(b_{r,s+1})$ and $a_{r-1,s+1}=d_{r,s+1}(b_{r,s+1})+\delta_{r-1,s+2}(b_{r-1,s+2})$. With the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-module-double-complex] ($dd=0$, $\delta\delta=0$, $\delta_{p-1,q}d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\delta_{p,q}$ for all $p,q$, zero modules and maps outside the first quadrant), $d_{r,s}(a_{r,s})=d_{r,s}d_{r+1,s}(b_{r+1,s})+d_{r,s}\delta_{r,s+1}(b_{r,s+1})=d_{r,s}\delta_{r,s+1}(b_{r,s+1})$ and $\delta_{r-1,s+1}(a_{r-1,s+1})=\delta_{r-1,s+1}d_{r,s+1}(b_{r,s+1})+\delta_{r-1,s+1}\delta_{r-1,s+2}(b_{r-1,s+2})=\delta_{r-1,s+1}d_{r,s+1}(b_{r,s+1})$, and these agree by the commuting square at $(r,s+1)$. So $a\in Z_n(A)$. (On a generator — $b$ concentrated at one place $(p,q)$, i.e. the tuple with $\delta b$ at $(p,q-1)$ and $db$ at $(p-1,q)$ — this is the check of the three adjacent conditions $d(\delta b)=\delta(db)$, $d(0)=0=\delta(\delta b)$, $d(db)=0=\delta(0)$.) Hence $Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A)=B_n(A)$ and $\mathbf H_n(A)=Z_n(A)/B_n(A)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18416-18449 (the zig-zags, the displayed set $d(a_{i+1,0})+\delta(a_{i,1}),\dots$, and 'Naturally, we divide out by trivial zig-zags'); the inclusion is left implicit there

proof.text: (b) Let $a\in Z_n(A)$ and $r\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $r+s=n$. Since $\Phi$ commutes with $d$ and $\delta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-double-complex], $d_{r,s}(\Phi_{r,s}a_{r,s})=\Phi_{r-1,s}(d_{r,s}a_{r,s})=\Phi_{r-1,s}(\delta_{r-1,s+1}a_{r-1,s+1})=\delta_{r-1,s+1}(\Phi_{r-1,s+1}a_{r-1,s+1})$, so $\Phi(a)\in Z_n(B)$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. For $b\in T_{n+1}(A)$ and $p+q=n$: $\Phi(D_{n+1}b)_{p,q}=\Phi_{p,q}(d_{p+1,q}b_{p+1,q}+\delta_{p,q+1}b_{p,q+1})=d_{p+1,q}\Phi_{p+1,q}(b_{p+1,q})+\delta_{p,q+1}\Phi_{p,q+1}(b_{p,q+1})=D_{n+1}(\Phi b)_{p,q}$ by linearity of $\Phi_{p,q}$ and the two commutation rules (at the boundary both sides are $0$ by the zero convention). Hence $\Phi(B_n(A))=\Phi D_{n+1}(T_{n+1}(A))=D_{n+1}(\Phi(T_{n+1}(A)))\subseteq D_{n+1}(T_{n+1}(B))=B_n(B)$. The componentwise map $\Phi:T_n(A)\to T_n(B)$ is $R$-linear, since each $\Phi_{p,q}$ is.

proof.text: (c) By (b) the componentwise map restricts to an $R$-linear map $\Phi_Z:Z_n(A)\to Z_n(B)$, and by (a) (for $A$ and $B$) $B_n(A)$ and $B_n(B)$ are submodules of $Z_n(A)$ and $Z_n(B)$ with $\Phi_Z(B_n(A))\subseteq B_n(B)$ by (b). By (a), $\mathbf H_n(A)=Z_n(A)/B_n(A)$ and $\mathbf H_n(B)=Z_n(B)/B_n(B)$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], with quotient maps $a\mapsto[a]$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-module-induced-map] applied to $f=\Phi_Z$, $N=B_n(A)$, $N'=B_n(B)$ gives a unique $R$-linear $\mathbf H_n(\Phi)=\overline{\Phi_Z}$ with $\mathbf H_n(\Phi)([a])=[\Phi(a)]$ for all $a\in Z_n(A)$.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph before Lemma Tag 00M1, lines 18391-18395, and proof of 00M1, lines 18416-18449 (the quotient $\mathbf H_i(A)$); written out here

proof.text: (d) Morphisms compose componentwise and the identity is $(\mathrm{id}_{A_{p,q}})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-double-complex], so on $T_n$, and hence on $Z_n$, $(\Psi\circ\Phi)_Z=\Psi_Z\circ\Phi_Z$ and $(\mathrm{id}_A)_Z=\mathrm{id}_{Z_n(A)}$. By (c), $\mathbf H_n(\Psi\circ\Phi)=\overline{\Psi_Z\circ\Phi_Z}$ and $\mathbf H_n(\mathrm{id}_A)=\overline{\mathrm{id}_{Z_n(A)}}$ (quotients by $B_n(A)$, $B_n(B)$, $B_n(C)$); clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-module-induced-map] gives $\overline{\Psi_Z\circ\Phi_Z}=\overline{\Psi_Z}\circ\overline{\Phi_Z}=\mathbf H_n(\Psi)\circ\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$ and $\overline{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf H_n(A)}$.

lean.statement: theorem zigzagModule_functorial {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (A B C : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ)) (Φ : A ⟶ B) (Ψ : B ⟶ C) (n : ℕ) : zigzagBoundaries A n ≤ zigzagCycles A n ∧ zigzagCycles A n ⊓ zigzagBoundaries A n = zigzagBoundaries A n ∧ (zigzagCycles A n).map (zigzagTotalMap Φ n) ≤ zigzagCycles B n ∧ (zigzagTotalMap Φ n).comp (zigzagBoundary A n) = (zigzagBoundary B n).comp (zigzagTotalMap Φ (n + 1)) ∧ (zigzagBoundaries A n).map (zigzagTotalMap Φ n) ≤ zigzagBoundaries B n ∧ (∀ (a : zigzagCycles A n) (b : zigzagCycles B n), b.val = zigzagTotalMap Φ n a.val → zigzagMap Φ n (Submodule.Quotient.mk a) = Submodule.Quotient.mk b) ∧ (∀ f : zigzagModule A n →ₗ[R] zigzagModule B n, (∀ (a : zigzagCycles A n) (b : zigzagCycles B n), b.val = zigzagTotalMap Φ n a.val → f (Submodule.Quotient.mk a) = Submodule.Quotient.mk b) → f = zigzagMap Φ n) ∧ zigzagMap (Φ ≫ Ψ) n = (zigzagMap Ψ n).comp (zigzagMap Φ n) ∧ zigzagMap (𝟙 A) n = LinearMap.id
